Five changes targeting the first 7 minutes: (1) QueueComBlueprint labs-first reorder so both labs build before mexes/winds; (2) target_e_grid raised from 1 to 2 for more concurrent energy grids; (3) energy stall threshold cut from 900 to 300 frames; (4) energy float cap raised from 0.70 to 0.85; (5) commander guards con bot 2 after com_starter. Stock com_starter.lua blueprint builds the air lab (corap) as item #27 of 46 in the commander's serial solo build queue, so the entire automated mex-grid expansion engine (StartAirExpansion/TryExpand, which only starts once the air lab exists) sat idle for minutes behind hand-placed mexes/winds the commander was building alone with its ~300 BP. Added BuildOrderedComLayout() in macro_controller.lua which takes a copy of COM_STARTER.layout and moves the corap entry to immediately follow corlab (bot lab), without touching the shared blueprint file itself so baseline_001 is unaffected. Informed by build_order_sim.py's balanced-mode optimizer, which favors unlocking BP-generating infrastructure early over exhausting a flat mex/wind list serially. Result: candidate had slightly lower metal income at 5 min (37.55 vs 39.92, the expected short-term cost of reordering) but dramatically higher income at 15 min (257.96 vs 139.46, ~1.85x), army value at 20 min (117904 vs 11183 metal-value, 773 vs 33 alive units), and total units built (1202 vs 876). Baseline also hoarded 1631 metal at 15 min vs candidate's 59, indicating baseline's BP was underutilized while candidate's freed-up expansion engine kept spending effectively.

User observed that in test matches both armies' node-curve contact lines converge on the same contested midpoint and grind past each other there, leaving the wide-open map sides undefended -- units sent along a flank could walk straight into the enemy base. Implemented a weak-spot detector in unit_controller.lua: every 5s enemy-scan tick, visible enemies are bucketed into lateral bins across (and slightly beyond) the contact line's width; if one bin has far fewer enemies than the rest (<=40% of the average, with a minimum 6-enemy sample), that lateral corridor is flagged as a weak spot. A fast-unit slice of the wing pool (up to 25% of total army metal value, gated on the main thrust force already meeting ADVANCE_MIN_UNITS so raiding never hollows out the line) is peeled off from wing-node duty and routed via a lateral waypoint through that corridor to a FIGHT order at the estimated enemy base (mirror of our own base across map centre, since the map is symmetric). Result: decisive win via commander/game_over kill. Army value at 10 min was 38110 (300 alive) vs baseline's 1352 (17 alive) -- baseline's combat-loss breakdown shows its economy buildings themselves destroyed (46x cornanotc, 2x coralab, 86x cormex, 94x corwin, 6x corvp), consistent with flank raiders reaching the base and tearing down production infrastructure rather than just trading in the centre, exactly the failure mode the user described. Units built 409 vs 324. No Lua errors from the new code; the reported 'Lua errors' were unrelated Picture-in-Picture Minimap widget-load log lines.

User watched a replay and saw the bot over-invest in build power while stalling on metal without expanding mexes fast enough, matching lessons_learned.md #3 (interrupts exist but don't elevate priority). blueprint_placer.lua is a shared file bot_testing.py copies from the repo root for both teams regardless of candidate contents, so the fix had to live in macro_controller.lua itself. Added: (1) RedirectBusyBuilderToMex, which stops a grid builder mid-blueprint and jumps it straight to the next unbuilt mex if metal is stalling (<17% storage) and it isn't already on a mex -- blueprint_placer only ever interrupted a busy builder for enemy threats, never for resource stalls; (2) AssistMexBuilds, which finds idle nanos within build range of a mex currently under construction and gives them a direct build order, since nanos placed as part of a grid are otherwise never given a follow-up order and just sit idle; (3) UpdateNanoPriorities, which uses GameCMD.PRIORITY to keep mex-assisting nanos at high priority and drops every other known nano to low priority during a metal stall so scarce metal goes to mex construction first, restoring everyone once the stall clears. Candidate won by commander kill: 538 vs 337 non-commander units built, army value 39585 (291 alive) vs baseline's 0 (fully wiped) at 10 min, and slightly better metal income at 5 min (42.29 vs 39.92).

Tuned three retreat/advance thresholds in unit_controller.lua, an area no prior run had touched (all previous tunes hit macro_controller's energy grid or lab_controller's poll rate/ratios). RETREAT_HP raised 0.15->0.30 so damaged units retreat before a hit that size can kill them mid-retreat, converting more near-deaths into free (time-only cost) recoverable survivors per game_mechanics.md 1.4; directly motivated by the replay-derived evidence entry where the bot lost 170 units in one 30s window and never recovered. ADVANCE_MIN_UNITS raised 5->10 so the contact line doesn't push forward with too thin a mass and get chewed up piecemeal. LOCAL_ENEMY_RADIUS raised 500->600 to match NODE_ENEMY_RADIUS, removing a MOVE/FIGHT contradiction in the 500-600 overlap band. Result: decisive win via commander kill, 810 vs 602 units built, army value 32519 (236 alive) vs baseline's 1260 (19 alive) at 10 min. Baseline's combat losses were dominated by cornanotc (122x, 28060 metal) and corraid (176x, 41360 metal), consistent with the base itself getting overrun rather than a clean battlefield trade.

User reported combat units getting very stretched out instead of fighting as a group. Root cause in AssignUnitPositions: it always spread units round-robin across the full thrust window (11 nodes) and all available wing nodes (up to ~21, spanning most of the ~3000-elmo contact line), regardless of actual unit count -- a small army of 10 units could end up one-per-node across the entire line. Two changes: (1) both thrust-node span and wing-node span are now capped by ceil(unitCount / UNITS_PER_NODE=4), centred/nearest to the existing window, so a small or medium force only occupies as many adjacent nodes as it has units to fill, only spreading to the full line once the army is large enough to justify it; wing candidates are sorted by distance to the thrust node so wing units cluster near the fight instead of scattering to the map edges. (2) Added a reinforcement muster pool: newly finished combat units are held out of line orders until either MUSTER_MIN_UNITS=4 have massed up or MUSTER_MAX_WAIT=900 frames (~30s) elapses, then released together, so reinforcements arrive and engage as a group instead of trickling out one at a time. Result: decisive win, 345 vs 233 units built, army value at 10 min 34911 (267 alive) vs baseline's 451 (8 alive, nearly wiped) -- baseline's per-unit combat losses (22x corshad for 3300 metal, 4x corvp for 2280 metal) show it lost fights badly, consistent with its units still arriving stretched thin. No functional Lua errors; the 4 flagged lines are unrelated Picture-in-Picture Minimap widget load log noise, same false-positive pattern noted in run 20260916_040637.

game_mechanics.md SS1.4/SS7 call Graverobber-type units mandatory and retreating low-HP main-army units a hard requirement, but neither existed in real form: the old retreat block MOVE-ordered critical-HP units to the commander's exact spawn point with no repair order ever issued to anything, so retreating units sat there unhealed indefinitely, and lab_controller.lua's generic fallback (used by corlab, the T1 bot lab, since it has no LAB_QUEUES entry) excluded every od.isBuilder buildOption -- which silently also excluded cornecro (Cortex's Graverobber: canresurrect=true, no buildOptions of its own, confirmed via UnitDefs[].canResurrect rather than name-matching) -- so no rez bot could ever be built regardless of what unit_controller.lua did. Fix spans both files: lab_controller.lua's GetBuildCache now special-cases od.canResurrect into its own bucket ahead of the isBuilder exclusion, and the generic fallback queues up to REZ_BOT_TARGET=2 of them, same pattern as the existing scout target. unit_controller.lua tracks rez bots separately (UnitFinished intercepts d.canResurrect before the isBuilder/isFactory early-return that used to make them invisible) and gives them a priority loop every ~2s: repair the most valuable nearby damaged ally (CMD.REPAIR targeting the unit, weighted by metal cost minus distance) > resurrect the nearest rezzable wreck within range (CMD.RESURRECT targeting featureID+Game.maxUnits, found via GetFeaturesInCylinder+GetFeatureResurrect) > hang back just behind the contact line's thrust node when idle. Critically wounded combat units (HP fraction < RETREAT_HP) now retreat toward the nearest living rez bot if one is within 2500 elmos instead of always making the long trip to the commander, connecting retreat and healing. Result vs baseline_001: game_over win via commander kill, 1805 vs 499 units built, army value 29614 (332 alive) vs baseline's 495 (3 alive) at 10 min. Two cornecro built and queued exactly at the REZ_BOT_TARGET cap (confirmed in headless.log), neither was a notable combat loss. No Lua errors from either modified file (only unrelated Picture-in-Picture Minimap widget-load log lines, consistent with prior runs). Baseline's early-game weakness (0 units built/alive at 1 min sanity check) is pre-existing and unrelated to this change.

Replaced the energy-grid ratchet in macro_controller.lua with a closed-loop energy/metal balance controller, targeting the measured energy overbuild in game_mechanics.md 11 (10-28% of energy production wasted while mex expansion fell 2.16x behind). Found two real defects, not just mistuning: (1) target_e_grid was compared against energy grids *currently building*, so each time one finished another claimed the next expansion slot - an unbounded drip of energy grids regardless of waste; it is now a cap on total grids ever queued via a monotonic eGridsQueuedTotal counter that cannot double-count a grid mid-transition between mostlyDone/done/pruned. (2) target_e_grid was a one-way ratchet raised by any 30s of pull>income and never lowered; since an energy grid consumes a mex expansion slot via pendingPlacements preempting pendingMexPlacements in TryAssign, every spurious increment permanently converted mex expansion into unusable energy. Now a stall only counts when demand outruns production AND storage is draining (<25%), so ordinary pull spikes at the start of a big build no longer ratchet it, and sustained waste (>8% of income for 45s, read from the engine's energyExcess return with a storage-saturation fallback) lowers it. Added an opportunity-cost guard requiring 3 producing mex grids per energy grid past the first, plus a ceiling of 6. Result: game_over win 1410 vs 919. Note baseline failed its own 1-min sanity check (0 units), so part of the margin is baseline weakness rather than this change.

All strategy_log entries above this line are confounded and must not be used to rank bots. bot_testing.py had three defects that all favoured whichever bot was passed as --bot1 (team 0): (1) setup_player was called with do_selfd=True for P1 only, so team 1 killed its own commander at duration-150s and, under deathmode=com, handed team 0 an automatic game_over win while also halving team 1's build time - this is the source of every game_over result and of the recurring ~2:1 units-built ratio; (2) fullview=1 does not give cross-team visibility in headless, yet _parse_logs read team 1's score from P0's blind log, undercounting slot 2 by ~5x (one mirror match: P0 said team 1 built 341, P1 said 1731) and producing the 'team 1: 0 units at 1 min' FAIL seen in every historical run; (3) the [DRAW_SCORE] adjudicator was computed inside one process so it always favoured its own team (same frame: P0 said mv0=194262 mv1=12599, P1 said mv0=9904 mv1=54920), and keyed off DRAW_FRAME=135000 which a 300s match never reaches. Found via a side-swap and a mirror match, controls that had never been run - the mirror showed a bot beating itself 2321 to 1143. All three are fixed; both teams now pass the 1-min sanity check. A genuine slot-0 advantage remains (mirror: mv0 198280 vs mv1 86072) but that one is a bot bug: macro_controller.lua only ever expands west, which is safe from team 0's top-left spawn and suicidal from team 1's bottom-right spawn.

Hypothesis NOT supported. Made macro_controller.lua's expansion direction spawn-relative via a towardEnemyX sign (+1/-1 from baseX vs Game.mapSizeX), mirroring the TryExpand forward filter, bot_starter placement, both VechT1_and_BotT2 production grids and the first initial mex grid, on the theory that always expanding west is safe from team 0's top-left spawn but aims expansion into contested ground from team 1's bottom-right spawn. Measured by mirror match against itself (the metric this change targets): army-value ratio got WORSE, 3.20x vs champion_v1's 2.30x. Caveat on both numbers: team 0 hits the ~2000 unit cap (nc0=1999) in every mirror run, so mv0 is saturated and the ratio is driven entirely by team 1's figure, which ranged 927-1627 across champion_v1 mirrors -- so single-run mirror ratios are noisy and this is at best weak evidence the change is harmful rather than merely useless. Not admitted. The slot-0 advantage remains unexplained; a capped-out team 0 means the mirror ratio needs a better metric (e.g. metal income at a fixed checkpoint) before this line of work is worth resuming.

SUPERSEDES the earlier WIN logged for 20260918_025426. That result (1410 vs 919) was measured under the broken harness and is void. Re-tested with ab_test.py (both slot orders, army metal value at frame 18000): baseline_001 leads in BOTH slots -- slot 0 essentially tied at 31758 vs 31673 (1.00x), slot 1 baseline ahead 29580 vs 25613 (1.15x). The closed-loop energy/metal balance controller is therefore a regression, not an improvement. The two defects it fixed in the baseline logic were real (target_e_grid compared against in-flight grids only, so energy grids drip forever; and a one-way ratchet that never fell), but capping total energy grids and gating them behind a 3-mex-per-energy-grid ratio evidently starves the bot of energy more than the overbuild cost it. The replay-derived premise in game_mechanics.md 11 -- that the bot overbuilds energy at the expense of mex -- may still be right; this particular correction is just too aggressive. A gentler version worth trying: keep the symmetric up/down controller and the drained-storage stall test, but drop the hard total cap and the E_MEX_RATIO gate, which are the two parts that can actively withhold energy the bot needs. Removed from champion_v1.

SUPERSEDES the earlier WIN logged for 20260915_221208 (air lab moved earlier in the commander build queue, originally credited with ~1.85x metal income at 15 min). That result was measured under the broken harness and is void. Re-tested with ab_test.py (both slot orders, army metal value at frame 18000): baseline_001 leads in BOTH slots -- slot 0 33650 vs 31146 (1.08x), slot 1 27257 vs 24549 (1.11x). Third consecutive historical WIN to fail re-validation, after 20260918_025426 (energy controller) and alongside my own 20260918_041530 (spawn-relative expansion). CAVEAT: these margins are only 1.08-1.15x and the noise floor of this metric has never been measured, so 'regression' here may just mean 'indistinguishable'. Running baseline_001 against itself through ab_test.py to establish what a true null result looks like before treating any of these verdicts as final.

RETRACTION. Ran baseline_001 against ITSELF through ab_test.py as a null control: it reported 'B is better -- it leads in BOTH slots', with slot 0 36167 vs 32233 (1.12x) and slot 1 28267 vs 26396 (1.07x), between two byte-identical bots. The run-to-run noise floor on army metal value at frame 18000 is therefore at least 1.12x, which is LARGER than every margin measured tonight. Consequently the three LOSS verdicts logged earlier this session -- 20260918_025426_REVALIDATED (energy controller, 1.00x/1.15x), 20260915_221208_REVALIDATED (air lab early, 1.08x/1.11x) and 20260918_041530 (spawn-relative expansion, judged on a single mirror ratio) -- are NOT supported. None of those changes has been shown to be a regression; they have been shown to be indistinguishable from noise with the evidence collected. The 'leads in both slot orders' criterion is by itself insufficient, because slot bias is systematic but run-to-run noise is not, and noise alone can produce a consistent-looking sweep. ab_test.py has been rewritten to repeat each condition (--repeat, default 3) and to declare a winner only when the two bots' runs do not overlap at all in a slot (min of one > max of the other), reporting NO DIFFERENCE DEMONSTRATED otherwise, and printing the observed within-condition spread alongside the verdict. Note what is NOT retracted: the three bot_testing.py defects found earlier are structural facts about the code (do_selfd=True passed for P1 only; team 1's score read from P0's blind log; [DRAW_SCORE] computed inside a single process), demonstrated by mechanism and by direct log comparison rather than by any margin, and they stand independently of this.

Energy controller re-tested with the rewritten ab_test.py on the quiet metric (metal income at frame 9000, noise floor 1.06x, 3 repeats per slot order). Result: NO DIFFERENCE DEMONSTRATED, and not marginally -- both bots produced exactly 40 metal/sec in all six runs in both slots, with observed spread 1.06x matching the predicted floor. This supersedes the earlier LOSS verdict, which was itself already retracted as noise. IMPORTANT CAVEAT about the metric rather than the bot: identical-to-the-digit figures mean frame 9000 is too early for this change to have engaged at all -- at 5 game-minutes both bots are still executing the same scripted commander opening, so the quiet window is quiet precisely because nothing has diverged yet. The project therefore has a structural measurability problem: frame 9000 has low noise but no signal, while frames 18000+ have real divergence but 1.44-1.68x noise. Increased [STATS] sampling from every 9000 frames to every 1800 (resources) and 3600 (army) so the signal and noise curves can be mapped per-frame and an optimal checkpoint chosen empirically, rather than guessed.

Mapped signal against noise at every sampled frame (checkpoint_map.py, 20260918_025426 vs baseline_001, 3 repeats, dense sampling). Result: signal/noise is BELOW 1.0 at every frame for both metrics -- 1.00 at best, falling to 0.31 by frame 36000. The energy controller's effect is real but tiny (signal reaches 1.42x by frame 36000) while noise there has reached 4.50x, so it is unmeasurable on this harness at any checkpoint and rerunning cannot fix that. Two useful by-products. (1) Army value is QUIETER than metal income in the early-to-mid window (1.07-1.14 at frames 3600-14400 vs income's 1.18-1.30), the opposite of the expectation that combat losses make it dirtier -- income is spiky because it tracks instantaneous build-power draw. ab_test.py's default is now army value at frame 14400, the latest point still under ~1.15x noise, giving a detectable effect size of roughly 15-20%. (2) Noise grows steeply with match length (army 1.09 at frame 3600 to 2.00 at 36000), so a longer match is a worse measurement -- raising --duration actively hurts. Caveat: floors are n=3 and themselves uncertain; frame 18000 measured 1.50x on one run and 1.20x on another.

Con bot 1 CMD_GUARDs the commander for the first 5 game-minutes instead of building the perimeter nano grid, on the theory that the commander's serial ~44-item com_starter queue is the opening's critical path and a second builder's BP would shorten it. Tested with ab_test.py on army value at frame 14400 (3 repeats): NO DIFFERENCE DEMONSTRATED, slot 0 19132 vs 19490 and slot 1 16237 vs 15739, both overlapping; the income cross-check at frame 9000 moved only 41 to 42. Diagnosing WHY produced the valuable result: stored metal averages 592, 375, 183, 57 at minutes 1-4, i.e. the bot burns its starting stock to nearly nothing and is METAL-limited, so the build power already present is idle waiting on metal and adding more cannot help. The same series then shows 646, 1544, 2258, 2077 at minutes 7-10 -- metal piling up unspent, i.e. BP-limited. The opening therefore has two phases with opposite bottlenecks, and this change was applied to the wrong one. Rule recorded in lessons_learned.md: minutes 1-6 improve only via more metal sooner (earlier mexes, less non-mex spending, never more builders); minutes 7+ improve only via more places to spend metal (parallel jobs, expansion slots, production). Candidate not admitted.

Bought an extra air con whenever stored metal exceeded 800 after minute 6 (cap 8, one per 30s), to convert the measured minute-7+ metal surplus into expansion capacity. ab_test.py on army value at frame 14400: NO DIFFERENCE DEMONSTRATED. The diagnostic is the valuable part: checking stored metal directly shows the change made hoarding WORSE, not better -- slot-0 stored metal ran ABOVE baseline throughout (minute 8: 1143 vs 1008; minute 10: 1036 vs 871; minute 11: 4071 vs 2667, 1.53x). If the mechanism had worked, A's stored metal would sit below B's. Extra cons therefore did not turn into extra grids, which refutes the premise: expansion is limited by available PLACEMENTS, not by air cons, so buying cons just produces idle aircraft while metal keeps piling up. This was the explicit risk flagged in the candidate's GOAL.md. Corollary worth acting on: both bots hoard 2667-4071 metal by minute 11, so the surplus is real and large and the true bottleneck is the number of valid build jobs. A prime suspect is TryExpand's half-plane filter (anchorX <= baseX + GRID_SPACING), which restricts mex-grid expansion to one side of the base and so roughly halves the placements that can ever exist. Candidate not admitted.

Removed TryExpand's half-plane filter (anchorX <= baseX + GRID_SPACING) so mex grids can be placed in all directions. ab_test.py verdict at frame 14400 was NO DIFFERENCE DEMONSTRATED because slot 1 overlapped, BUT slot 0 was clearly ahead with no overlap (19823-20402 vs 18231-19128) and the mechanism demonstrably fired, unlike the previous two candidates. Direct check of stored metal and income: in slot 0 A's stored metal falls below baseline at minutes 8-10 (1137 vs 2008 at minute 10) while income runs consistently higher, reaching 400.9 vs 343.3 at minute 12, +17 percent -- surplus genuinely converted into economy. In slot 1 the mechanism also fired but income was mixed (worse at minutes 7-9, better at 10-11). The asymmetry has a clean mechanical explanation: the filter was POSITIONALLY biased, not merely directional. Team 0 spawns at x=2400 so anchorX <= baseX+480 left it almost no placements; team 1 spawns at x=9648 so the same rule already granted it most of the map. Lifting the filter is therefore a large gain for slot 0 and close to a no-op for slot 1, which is exactly the observed pattern and is consistent with this being a genuine improvement rather than noise. Escalating to --repeat 5 for a decisive answer on slot 1 rather than admitting on slot 0 alone.

Concentrated the army (THRUST_FRAC 0.55->0.85, THRUST_NODE_HALF 5->3) after a replay showed 1.88 damage ratio but 393 units lost. ab_test.py at --checkpoint 27000 crashed on the first slot-1 match (bot_testing.py exit 1); a manual rerun of that match completed but only reached frame ~26600 in 300s, so frame 27000 is not reachable at default duration. NO VERDICT: the change is unmeasured, not a win or regression. Also renamed DISTRIBUTED_BO to DRAGON_BOT.
